```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(mgm)

library(networktools)

library(gridExtra)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# Path configuration (edit here; every path below references these)
# ==============================================================================

data_proc_dir  <- here::here('Data', 'Processed')    # intermediate outputs

out_fig_dir    <- here::here('Output', '01-Env-health', 'Figures')
```

```{r}
# --- 4. Run safety check ---

  msg <- paste0(
    "Column count mismatch!\n",
    "------------------------------\n",
    "Current number of columns: ", current_cols, "\n",
    "Number of new variable names: ", target_cols, "\n",
    "Difference: ", current_cols - target_cols, "\n",
    "------------------------------\n",
    "Check whether the select() statement is missing variables, or new_colnames is defined incorrectly."
  )
  stop(msg)
```

# Data input
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 1: Variable definition, selection and renaming
# ==============================================================================
library(dplyr)
library(missForest)
library(psych)
library(tibble)

# 1.1 Define original variable names (list kept as provided)
e_orig_names <- c("e_city", "e_dist", "e_metro", "e_Bus", "e_wlkgrn", "e_wvgrn", "e_wlkblu", "e_wvblu",
                  "e_facil", "e_Price", "e_work", "e_eduEL", "e_comCen", "e_medAc", "e_alcig", 
                  "e_neiAl", "e_neiLow", "e_neiSoci", "e_themCo", "e_clim", "e_poll", "e_lighting",
                  "e_privacy", "e_narrow", "e_PA", "e_sleep", "e_heaFood", "e_lifestyle", "e_safe")

l_orig_names <- c('l_palgt', 'l_pamed', 'l_pahig', 'l_lgtdur', 'l_meddur', 'l_higdur', 
                  'l_sitdur', 'l_leidur', "l_eathealth", 'l_eatout', 'l_smoking', 
                  'l_drinking', "l_medictest", "l_adaptCop", "l_med_seek", "l_info_seek")

mh_orig_names <- c('m_conc', 'm_wea', 'm_pos', 'm_app', 'm_neg', 'm_est', 'm_res', 'm_eat')
ph_orig_names <- c("p_energy","p_pain","p_medD","p_genH","p_sleep","p_daily","p_work","p_mobility")
sh_orig_names <- c("SS_1","SS_2","SS_3","SS_4","SS_5","SS_6","SS_7","SS_8")
ses_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Edu", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "DurRes", "LivArea")

# 1.2 Select data
all_vars_for_imputation <- c(e_orig_names, l_orig_names, mh_orig_names, ph_orig_names, sh_orig_names, ses_vars)

# Check that the variables exist
if(!all(all_vars_for_imputation %in% colnames(df))) {
  missing_vars <- all_vars_for_imputation[!all_vars_for_imputation %in% colnames(df)]
  stop(paste("Error: the data frame is missing the following columns:", paste(missing_vars, collapse=", ")))
}

df_analysis <- df[, all_vars_for_imputation]

# 1.3 Rename (build old-to-new name mapping)
# Generate new names
e_item_names <- paste0("E", 1:length(e_orig_names))
l_item_names <- paste0("L", 1:length(l_orig_names))
mh_item_names <- paste0("M", 1:length(mh_orig_names))
ph_item_names <- paste0("P", 1:length(ph_orig_names))
sh_item_names <- paste0("S", 1:length(sh_orig_names))

# Apply the renaming
names(df_analysis)[match(e_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- e_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(l_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- l_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(mh_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- mh_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(ph_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- ph_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(sh_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- sh_item_names

# Reorder (E, L, M, P, S, SES)
core_node_names <- c(e_item_names, l_item_names, mh_item_names, ph_item_names, sh_item_names)
all_vars_clean <- c(core_node_names, ses_vars)
df_analysis <- df_analysis[, all_vars_clean]

message("Variable selection and renaming complete.")

# ==============================================================================
# Step 2: Descriptive statistics of the raw data (pre-imputation)
# ==============================================================================

# Define a generic descriptive-statistics function
get_descriptive_stats <- function(data, label="Stats") {
  
  data_num <- data %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(.)))
  
  # Use psych::describe for basic statistics
  desc <- psych::describe(data_num, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
    dplyr::select(Variable, mean, sd, min, max, skew)
  
  missing_counts <- sapply(data, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
  var_types <- sapply(data, function(x) class(x)[1])
  
  # Merge
  final_tab <- desc %>%
    mutate(
      Missing_N = missing_counts[Variable],
      Missing_Pct = round(Missing_N / nrow(data) * 100, 2),
      Type = var_types[Variable]
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(mean, sd, skew), ~round(., 3))) # keep 3 decimal places
  
  return(final_tab)
}

# 2.1 Ensure SES variables have the right format (for statistics)
ses_factor_vars <- c("Gender", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "Edu")
df_raw_stat <- df_analysis
for(col in ses_factor_vars) {
  if(col %in% names(df_raw_stat)) df_raw_stat[[col]] <- as.factor(df_raw_stat[[col]])
}

# 2.2 Build and export the raw statistics table
stats_raw <- get_descriptive_stats(df_raw_stat)

# Export CSV
write.csv(stats_raw, file.path(out_tables_dir, "Table_Descriptive_Raw_Data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
message("Raw-data statistics table exported: Table_Descriptive_Raw_Data.csv")

# Print a preview (first few rows)
print(head(stats_raw))

# ==============================================================================
# Step 3: missForest imputation
# ==============================================================================

# 3.1 Prepare data for imputation (categorical variables must be factors)
df_for_imp <- df_analysis
for(col in ses_factor_vars) {
  df_for_imp[[col]] <- as.factor(df_for_imp[[col]])
}

message("\nStarting missForest imputation (ntree=500)... this may take a few minutes...")

# 3.2 Run the imputation
set.seed(123) # fix the random seed for reproducibility
imp_result <- missForest(df_for_imp, 
                         verbose = TRUE, 
                         ntree = 500,     
                         maxiter = 10)

# Extract the imputed data
df_clean <- imp_result$ximp

# 3.3 Print the error report
message("\nImputation complete. OOB error estimate:")
print(imp_result$OOBerror)

# ==============================================================================
# Step 4: Pre/post-imputation comparison report
# ==============================================================================

# 4.1 Build the post-imputation statistics table
stats_imp <- get_descriptive_stats(df_clean)

# 4.2 Merge for comparison
comparison_table <- stats_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, Raw_Mean = mean, Raw_SD = sd, Raw_Skew = skew, Missing_N) %>%
  left_join(
    stats_imp %>% dplyr::select(Variable, Imp_Mean = mean, Imp_SD = sd, Imp_Skew = skew),
    by = "Variable"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Diff = round(Imp_Mean - Raw_Mean, 4),
    SD_Diff = round(Imp_SD - Raw_SD, 4)
  )

# 4.3 Export the comparison table
write.csv(comparison_table, file.path(out_tables_dir, "Table_Imputation_Check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
message("Pre/post-imputation comparison table exported: Table_Imputation_Check.csv")

# 4.4 Check for large changes (warn if a mean shifts by more than 0.5)
large_changes <- comparison_table %>% filter(abs(Mean_Diff) > 0.5)
if(nrow(large_changes) > 0) {
  message("Warning: the following variables show a large mean change after imputation, please check:")
  print(large_changes$Variable)
} else {
  message("Check passed: no large mean shift between pre- and post-imputation.")
}

# ==============================================================================
# Step 5: Final output (prepare for the next splitting step)
# ==============================================================================

for(col in colnames(df_clean)) {
  if(is.factor(df_clean[[col]])) {
    df_clean[[col]] <- as.numeric(as.character(df_clean[[col]]))
    if(any(is.na(df_clean))) stop("Numeric conversion introduced NA")
  }
}

message("\nReady. df_clean is now a complete numeric data frame with no missing values.")
message("Continue with the Step 4 (data splitting) code.")
```


# advanced data process-df_clean
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 4: Data forking (SES dummy-variable control, fixed)
# ==============================================================================
# Key correction:

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

message("\n[Step 4] Running data forking (SES type-corrected version)...")

# --- 1. Variable definitions ---

all_items <- c(e_item_names, l_item_names, mh_item_names, ph_item_names, sh_item_names)
ses_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Edu", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "DurRes", "LivArea")

# Group A: treated as continuous numeric (includes low-to-high ordinal variables such as Edu)
ses_numeric_vars <- c("Age", "Edu", "DurRes", "LivArea") 

# Group B: must be treated as categorical factors (nominal + binary variables)
ses_factor_vars <- c("Gender", "Emp", "Imm", "CD")

# --- 2. Prepare the SES data frame (for lm regression) ---

ses_df_model <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(ses_vars)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ses_numeric_vars), ~as.numeric(as.character(.)))) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ses_factor_vars), ~as.factor(.)))

str(ses_df_model)

# --- 3. Prepare the item data ---
df_clean_num <- as.data.frame(df_clean) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(all_items), ~as.numeric(as.character(.))))


# --- 4. Run the forking ---

# === Branch A: df_raw_bggm (for BGGM) ===
df_raw_bggm <- df_clean_num 
message("df_raw_bggm ready.")


# === Branch B: df_resid (for DAG) ===
df_resid <- df_clean_num # copy the structure

message("Computing residuals (dummies handled automatically)...")

for(item in all_items) {
  tmp_data <- cbind(Y_Target = df_clean_num[[item]], ses_df_model)
  
  fit <- lm(Y_Target ~ ., data = tmp_data, na.action = na.exclude)
  
  df_resid[[item]] <- residuals(fit)
}

message("df_resid ready (SES categorical variables correctly controlled).")


# --- 5. Compute composite scores ---
calc_score <- function(data, vars) {
  if(length(vars) == 0) return(rep(NA, nrow(data)))
  rowMeans(data[, vars, drop=FALSE], na.rm=TRUE)
}

df_scores <- df_resid %>%
  mutate(
    E_Score = calc_score(., e_item_names),
    L_Score = calc_score(., l_item_names),
    M_Score = calc_score(., mh_item_names),
    P_Score = calc_score(., ph_item_names),
    S_Score = calc_score(., sh_item_names),
    H_Score_Total = rowMeans(cbind(M_Score, P_Score, S_Score), na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(E_Score, L_Score, M_Score, P_Score, S_Score, H_Score_Total), ~as.numeric(scale(.))))

message("df_scores ready.")

# ==============================================================================
# Save
# ==============================================================================
continuous_items <- c() 

save(df_clean_num, df_raw_bggm, df_resid, df_scores, 
     ses_df_model,
     continuous_items,
     file = file.path(data_proc_dir, "Data_Forked_Step4.RData"))

message("\nData updated and saved to Data_Forked_Step4.RData")


```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 5C: Mediation analysis (result extraction - select-error fix)
# ==============================================================================
library(lavaan)
library(dplyr)

message("\n[Step 5C] Running the mediation analysis (lavaan)...")

# 1. Define the function
run_mediation <- function(data, outcome_var, label) {
  model <- paste0('
    L_Score ~ a * E_Score
    ', outcome_var, ' ~ b * L_Score + c_prime * E_Score
    indirect := a * b
    total    := c_prime + (a * b)
    pm       := indirect / total
  ')
  
  set.seed(1234) 
  fit <- sem(model, data = data, se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000)
  return(list(fit = fit, label = label, outcome = outcome_var))
}

# 2. Run in batch and extract the results
med_models <- list()
outcomes <- list(
  "Total_Health"    = "H_Score_Total",
  "Mental_Health"   = "M_Score",
  "Physical_Health" = "P_Score",
  "Social_Health"   = "S_Score"
)

summary_list <- list()

for(name in names(outcomes)) {
  message(paste("   ⏳ Running model:", name))
  
  res <- run_mediation(df_scores, outcomes[[name]], name)
  med_models[[name]] <- res 
  
  # --- Result extraction (error-fixed) ---
  est <- parameterEstimates(res$fit, standardized = TRUE, boot.ci.type = "perc") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    
    dplyr::filter(label %in% c("a", "b", "c_prime", "indirect", "total", "pm")) %>%
    
    dplyr::mutate(
      Path_Label = case_when(
        label == "a" ~ "Environment -> Lifestyle",
        label == "b" ~ paste0("Lifestyle -> ", name),
        label == "c_prime" ~ paste0("Environment -> ", name, " (Direct)"),
        label == "indirect" ~ paste0("Env -> Life -> ", name, " (Mediation)"),
        label == "total" ~ paste0("Environment -> ", name, " (Total)"),
        label == "pm" ~ "% Mediation",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) %>%
    
    dplyr::mutate(
      CI_Str = paste0("[", sprintf("%.3f", ci.lower), ", ", sprintf("%.3f", ci.upper), "]")
    ) %>%
    
    dplyr::select(
      Model = rhs, # temporary placeholder
      `Path / Effect` = label,
      `Path Label` = Path_Label,
      `Standardized Coefficient (β)` = std.all,
      `Standard Error (SE)` = se,
      `P` = pvalue,
      `95% CI (Bootstrap)` = CI_Str
    ) %>%
    
    dplyr::mutate(
      Model = name,
      `Standardized Coefficient (β)` = round(`Standardized Coefficient (β)`, 3),
      `Standard Error (SE)` = round(`Standard Error (SE)`, 3),
      `P` = sprintf("%.3f", `P`)
    )
  
  summary_list[[name]] <- est
}

# 3. Combine and export
final_med_tab <- bind_rows(summary_list)

print(head(final_med_tab))

write.csv(final_med_tab, file.path(out_tables_dir, "Table_Mediation_Results_Final_Beta.csv"), row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
message("Results exported: Table_Mediation_Results_Final_Beta.csv")
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 5D: Mediation-model visualisation (with residual arrows)
# ==============================================================================
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(patchwork)

message("\n[Step 5D] Building the mediation-model visualisation (with residual arrows)...")

# Inspect the data structure of the Total_Health model
message("Printout of the model results below:")
print(summary_list[["Total_Health"]])

# 1. Extract path coefficients from the results (unchanged)
extract_path_coefficients <- function(model_name) {
  model_data <- summary_list[[model_name]]
  
  paths <- data.frame(
    from = c("E_Score", "L_Score", "E_Score"),
    to = c("L_Score", model_name, model_name),
    path_type = c("E→L", "L→Y", "E→Y"),
    beta = c(
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "a") %>% pull(`Standardized Coefficient (β)`),
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "b") %>% pull(`Standardized Coefficient (β)`),
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "c_prime") %>% pull(`Standardized Coefficient (β)`)
    ),
    p_value = c(
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "a") %>% pull(P) %>% as.numeric(),
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "b") %>% pull(P) %>% as.numeric(),
      model_data %>% filter(`Path / Effect` == "c_prime") %>% pull(P) %>% as.numeric()
    )
  )
  
  paths$label <- sprintf("β = %.3f%s", 
                         paths$beta,
                         ifelse(paths$p_value < 0.001, "***",
                                ifelse(paths$p_value < 0.01, "**",
                                       ifelse(paths$p_value < 0.05, "*", ""))))
  return(paths)
}

# 2. Function to draw the mediation-model diagram (auto-computes residuals)
plot_mediation_model <- function(model_name, title_suffix = "") {
  
  model_data <- summary_list[[model_name]]
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  paths <- extract_path_coefficients(model_name)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # B. Auto-compute residual / unexplained variance
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  # 1. Extract the coefficient values
  beta_a <- paths %>% filter(path_type == "E→L") %>% pull(beta)
  beta_b <- paths %>% filter(path_type == "L→Y") %>% pull(beta)
  beta_c_prime <- paths %>% filter(path_type == "E→Y") %>% pull(beta)
  
  # 2. Compute the residual for the mediator (Lifestyle)
  # Formula: Var(L) = beta_a^2 * Var(E) + Var(e_L) => 1 = beta_a^2 + e^2
  r2_med <- beta_a^2
  e_med <- sqrt(max(0, 1 - r2_med)) # max(0,...) guards against a negative from float error
  
  # 3. Compute the residual for the outcome (Health)
  # Formula: Var(Y) = Explained_Var + Var(e_Y)
  # Explained_Var = beta_c'^2 + beta_b^2 + 2 * beta_c' * beta_b * correlation(E,L)
  r2_out <- beta_c_prime^2 + beta_b^2 + (2 * beta_c_prime * beta_b * beta_a)
  e_out <- sqrt(max(0, 1 - r2_out))
  
  message(paste0("   [auto] ", model_name, 
                 " | R2_Med=", round(r2_med,3), " (e=", round(e_med,2), ")",
                 " | R2_Out=", round(r2_out,3), " (e=", round(e_out,2), ")"))

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # C. Define residual-arrow positions
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  error_data <- data.frame(
    name = c("Lifestyle", get_friendly_name(model_name)),
    x_start = c(2.9, 2.9),  # arrow start
    x_end   = c(2.4, 2.4),  # arrow end (touching the box edge)
    y       = c(2, 1),      # same height as the nodes
    label   = c(sprintf("%.2f", e_med), sprintf("%.2f", e_out))
  )
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # D. Set node positions
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  nodes <- data.frame(
    name = c("Environment", "Lifestyle", get_friendly_name(model_name)),
    x = c(1, 2, 2),
    y = c(2, 2, 1)
  )
  
  edges <- data.frame(
    from = c("Environment", "Lifestyle", "Environment"),
    to = c("Lifestyle", get_friendly_name(model_name), get_friendly_name(model_name)),
    beta = paths$beta,
    path_type = paths$path_type,
    label = paths$label
  ) %>%
    left_join(nodes, by = c("from" = "name")) %>%
    rename(x_start = x, y_start = y) %>%
    left_join(nodes, by = c("to" = "name")) %>%
    rename(x_end = x, y_end = y)
  
  color_mapping <- c("E→L"="#87CEEB", "L→Y"="#FFB6C1", "E→Y"="#90EE90")
  edges$linewidth <- abs(edges$beta) * 5
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # E. Plot (ggplot2)
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  p <- ggplot() +
    # 1. Draw the node boxes
    geom_rect(data = nodes, 
              aes(xmin = x - 0.4, xmax = x + 0.4, 
                  ymin = y - 0.15, ymax = y + 0.15),
              fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    
    # 2. Draw the node labels
    geom_text(data = nodes, 
              aes(x = x, y = y, label = name),
              size = 4.5, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5) +
    
    # --- Draw residual arrows (grey, right to left) ---
    geom_segment(data = error_data,
                 aes(x = x_start, y = y, xend = x_end, yend = y),
                 color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.8,
                 arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.15, "inches"))) +
    
    # --- Draw residual values (to the right of the arrow tail) ---
    geom_text(data = error_data,
              aes(x = x_start + 0.05, y = y, label = label),
              size = 4, color = "gray40", hjust = 0, fontface = "italic") +
    
    # 3. Draw the main paths (with arrows)
    geom_segment(data = edges,
                 aes(x = x_start, y = y_start, xend = x_end, yend = y_end,
                     color = path_type, linewidth = linewidth),
                 arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.2, "inches")),
                 show.legend = FALSE) +
    
    # 4. Main-path labels
    geom_label(data = edges,
               aes(x = (x_start + x_end) / 2, y = (y_start + y_end) / 2, label = label),
               size = 3.5, fill = "white", alpha = 0.8, label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
    
    scale_color_manual(values = color_mapping) +
    scale_linewidth_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3)) +
    
    xlim(0.5, 3.3) + 
    ylim(0.5, 2.5) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, color = "gray60")
    ) +
    
    labs(title = paste("Mediation Model:", title_suffix),
         subtitle = "Standardized Path Coefficients & Calc. Residuals",
         caption = "Residuals calculated from standardized betas")
  
  return(p)
}

get_friendly_name <- function(model_name) {
  case_when(
    model_name == "Total_Health" ~ "Total Health",
    model_name == "Mental_Health" ~ "Mental Health",
    model_name == "Physical_Health" ~ "Physical Health",
    model_name == "Social_Health" ~ "Social Health",
    TRUE ~ model_name
  )
}

# 3. Loop over models: plot and save (unchanged)
model_titles <- c(
  "Total_Health" = "Total Health (H_Score_Total)",
  "Mental_Health" = "Mental Health (M_Score)",
  "Physical_Health" = "Physical Health (P_Score)",
  "Social_Health" = "Social Health (S_Score)"
)

mediation_plots <- list()

for (model_name in names(model_titles)) {
  message(paste("   📊 Creating plot for:", model_name))
  p <- plot_mediation_model(model_name, model_titles[[model_name]])
  mediation_plots[[model_name]] <- p
  ggsave(paste0("Mediation_Model_", model_name, ".pdf"), p, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300) # a bit wider to fit the right-side arrows
}

# 4. Combined figure (unchanged)
combined_title <- "Mediation Models: Environment → Lifestyle → Health Outcomes"
combined_plot <- (mediation_plots[["Total_Health"]] + mediation_plots[["Mental_Health"]]) / 
  (mediation_plots[["Physical_Health"]] + mediation_plots[["Social_Health"]]) +
  plot_annotation(title = combined_title, 
                  subtitle = "Gray arrows indicate residual path coefficients (unexplained variance)",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16)))

ggsave("Combined_Mediation_Models.pdf", combined_plot, width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300)

message("\nVisualisation complete. Residual arrows (e) added in the reference style.")
```

# Analysis 2: BGGM / SES controlled and uncontrolled - 0105
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 6: BGGM network analysis (sign-in-plot fix)
# ==============================================================================
library(BGGM)
library(qgraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggridges)
library(networktools)
library(gridExtra)

# --- 1. Basic configuration ---
out_dir <- out_fig_dir  # write to this project's Figures directory

ITER_NUM <- 5000 

e_names <- e_item_names
l_names <- l_item_names
multi_models <- list(
  "Mental_Health"   = mh_item_names, 
  "Physical_Health" = ph_item_names, 
  "Social_Health"   = sh_item_names
)

# --- Visual parameters ---
custom_node_colors <- c("Environment"="#AEC7E8", "Lifestyle"="#98DF8A", 
                        "Mental_Health"="#D8BFD8", "Physical_Health"="#FFBB78", "Social_Health"="#FFB6C1")
bridge_highlight_color <- "#FFD700" 
vsize_fixed <- 4
label_size_fixed <- 0.8  
vBorder_color <- rep("gray30", 100); vBorder_width <- rep(1, 100)

if(!exists("df_raw_bggm") || !exists("df_resid")) stop("Error: data sources not found.")

message("Configuration loaded. Fixed the loss of sign in pcor_adj.")



# ==============================================================================
# Core analysis function (force signed weights)
# ==============================================================================
run_bggm_full_metrics <- function(data_raw_full, data_resid_full, node_names, groups_list, model_label, out_dir, n_iter = ITER_NUM) {
  
  # --- 0. Data integrity check ---
  if(!all(node_names %in% colnames(data_raw_full))) {
    missing <- node_names[!node_names %in% colnames(data_raw_full)]
    stop(paste("Error: the following variables are missing from the data:", paste(missing, collapse=", ")))
  }
  
  set.seed(42)
  
  # --- 1. Prepare the data matrices ---
  Y_raw_mat <- as.matrix(data_raw_full[, node_names])
  Y_resid_mat <- as.matrix(data_resid_full[, node_names])
  mode(Y_raw_mat) <- "numeric"
  mode(Y_resid_mat) <- "numeric"
  
  # --- 2. BGGM estimation and selection ---
  fit_raw <- BGGM::estimate(Y = Y_raw_mat, iter = n_iter, progress = FALSE)
  fit_ctrl <- BGGM::estimate(Y = Y_resid_mat, iter = n_iter, progress = FALSE)
  
  sel_raw  <- BGGM::select(fit_raw,  cred = 0.99)
  sel_ctrl <- BGGM::select(fit_ctrl, cred = 0.99)
  
  # --- Robustly extract the 0/1 significance matrix ---
  get_sig_matrix <- function(bg_obj, label) {
    obj_names <- names(bg_obj)
    # Strategy 1: look for Adj_XX
    adj_candidate <- obj_names[grepl("^Adj_", obj_names)]
    if(length(adj_candidate) > 0) return(as.matrix(bg_obj[[adj_candidate[1]]]))
    # Strategy 2: look for Adj_cred
    if("Adj_cred" %in% obj_names) return(as.matrix(bg_obj$Adj_cred))
    # Strategy 3: look for pcor_adj
    if("pcor_adj" %in% obj_names) return(as.matrix(bg_obj$pcor_adj))
    
    message(paste("   ❌ [Debug] Available names in object:", paste(obj_names, collapse=", ")))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  mat_sig_raw  <- get_sig_matrix(sel_raw, "Raw")
  mat_sig_ctrl <- get_sig_matrix(sel_ctrl, "Control")
  
  if(is.null(mat_sig_raw) || is.null(mat_sig_ctrl)) {
    stop("BGGM Error: could not locate the adjacency matrix automatically.")
  }
  
  pcor_mat_raw <- fit_raw$pcor_mat
  pcor_mat_ctrl <- fit_ctrl$pcor_mat
  
  message(paste("   🔍 [Check] Raw Pcor Range:", paste(round(range(pcor_mat_raw),3), collapse=" to ")))
  
  adj_raw  <- as.matrix(pcor_mat_raw) * as.matrix(mat_sig_raw)
  adj_ctrl <- as.matrix(pcor_mat_ctrl) * as.matrix(mat_sig_ctrl)
  
  colnames(adj_raw) <- rownames(adj_raw) <- node_names
  colnames(adj_ctrl) <- rownames(adj_ctrl) <- node_names
  
  write.csv(adj_ctrl, file.path(out_dir, paste0("adj_matrix_BGGM_", model_label, "_Pearson_Resid.csv")))
  
  # Compute correlations
  vals_raw <- adj_raw[upper.tri(adj_raw)]
  vals_ctrl <- adj_ctrl[upper.tri(adj_ctrl)]
  
  if(sd(vals_raw) == 0 || sd(vals_ctrl) == 0) {
    cor_r <- 0 
  } else {
    cor_r <- cor(vals_raw, vals_ctrl)
  }
  
  # --- 3. Prepare the community vector needed for the metrics ---
  node_count <- length(node_names)
  community_chr <- character(node_count)
  
  for (g_name in names(groups_list)) { 
    g_indices <- groups_list[[g_name]]
    valid_indices <- g_indices[g_indices <= node_count]
    if(length(valid_indices) > 0) {
      community_chr[valid_indices] <- g_name
    }
  }
  
  # --- 4. Compute bridge and node metrics ---
  br_res <- tryCatch({
    networktools::bridge(adj_ctrl, communities = community_chr, useCommunities = "all", directed = FALSE, nodes = node_names)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("   ⚠️ Bridge metrics calculation failed: ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if(!is.null(br_res)){
    val_bridge_ei <- br_res$`Bridge Expected Influence (1-step)` 
    val_bridge_str <- br_res$`Bridge Strength`                    
  } else {
    val_bridge_ei <- rep(0, node_count)
    val_bridge_str <- rep(0, node_count)
  }
  
  # Node Metrics
  val_node_ei <- colSums(adj_ctrl)       
  val_node_str <- colSums(abs(adj_ctrl)) 
  
  # --- 5. Highlight rule ---
  pos_candidates <- val_bridge_ei
  pos_candidates[pos_candidates <= 0] <- -Inf 
  
  if(all(pos_candidates == -Inf)){
    threshold <- Inf 
  } else {
    threshold <- quantile(pos_candidates[pos_candidates > -Inf], 0.8, na.rm=TRUE) 
  }
  
  top_nodes_idx <- which(val_bridge_ei >= threshold & val_bridge_ei > 0)
  
  node_colors_default <- unname(custom_node_colors[community_chr])
  node_colors_highlight <- node_colors_default
  if(length(top_nodes_idx) > 0) node_colors_highlight[top_nodes_idx] <- bridge_highlight_color
  
  # --- 6. Plotting function ---
  plot_lollipop <- function(vals, title, subtitle) {
    df <- data.frame(Node = node_names, Val = vals, Community = community_chr) %>% arrange(Val)
    df$Node <- factor(df$Node, levels = df$Node) 
    
    ggplot(df, aes(x=Node, y=Val, color=Community)) +
      geom_segment(aes(xend=Node, yend=0), color="grey") +
      geom_point(size=2.5) + coord_flip() +
      scale_color_manual(values = custom_node_colors) +
      labs(title=title, subtitle=subtitle, x="", y="Value") +
      theme_minimal() + 
      theme(legend.position="none", plot.title = element_text(size=10, face="bold"))
  }
  
  p1 <- plot_lollipop(val_bridge_ei, "Bridge Expected Influence", "Signed Sum")
  p2 <- plot_lollipop(val_bridge_str, "Bridge Strength", "Absolute Sum")
  p3 <- plot_lollipop(val_node_ei, "Node Expected Influence", "Signed Sum")
  p4 <- plot_lollipop(val_node_str, "Node Strength", "Absolute Sum")
  
  # --- 7. Return ---
  # Pre-compute the layout
  L_avg <- qgraph(adj_ctrl, layout="spring", DoNotPlot=TRUE)$layout
  
  return(list(
    adj_raw = adj_raw, adj_ctrl = adj_ctrl, cor_r = cor_r,
    p_matrix = list(p1, p2, p3, p4), 
    node_colors_default = node_colors_default,
    node_colors_highlight = node_colors_highlight,
    layout_spring = L_avg
  ))
}


# ==============================================================================
# Run the main loop
# ==============================================================================
message("\n🚀 STARTING BGGM ANALYSIS LOOP...")

pdf(file.path(out_dir, "Step6_BGGM_Results_FullMetrics.pdf"), width = 18, height = 12)

for(model_label in names(multi_models)){
```

# Bootnet stability analysis for all models
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# III. PHASE 3: STABILITY ANALYSIS (bootnet) - Updated for SES-Adjusted Residuals
# ==============================================================================
# Notes:
# 1. Use EBICglasso as a fast proxy for BGGM in the stability test.
# 2. Important: use df_resid (from Step 4), because SES effects have already been removed.

library(bootnet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

message("\n🚀 STARTING PHASE 3: STABILITY ANALYSIS FOR ALL MODELS")

# 1. Basic configuration and checks
if(!exists("out_dir")) out_dir <- out_fig_dir
if(!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Key check: ensure df_resid exists
if(!exists("df_resid")) {
  stop("Error: 'df_resid' not found. Run the Step 4 code first to generate the deconfounded residual data.")
}

# Loop: Mental -> Physical -> Social
for(model_label in names(multi_models)){
  
  message(paste("\n----------------------------------------------------"))
  message(paste(">>> [Phase 3] Testing Stability for:", model_label))
  message(paste("----------------------------------------------------"))
  
  # 2. Prepare data
  nodes_extra <- multi_models[[model_label]]
  target_vars <- c(e_names, l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  data_for_boot <- df_resid %>% dplyr::select(all_of(target_vars))
  
  # 3. Define bridge communities dynamically
  n_e <- length(e_names)
  n_l <- length(l_names)
  n_h <- length(nodes_extra)
  
  communities <- list(
    "Environment" = 1:n_e,
    "Lifestyle"   = (n_e + 1):(n_e + n_l),
    "Health"      = (n_e + n_l + 1):(n_e + n_l + n_h)
  )
  
  # 4. Run bootnet
  # 4.1 Estimate the base network (EBICglasso)
  message(paste("   👉 Estimating base network (EBICglasso on Residuals)..."))
  
  network_estimate <- estimateNetwork(
    data_for_boot, 
    default = "EBICglasso", 
    corMethod = "cor", 
    tuning = 0.5,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  # 4.2 Run case-dropping bootstrap
  message(paste("   👉 Running 1000 bootstraps (this takes time)..."))
  # Fix the bootnet seed
  set.seed(777)
  
  boot_res <- bootnet(
    network_estimate, 
    boots = 1000,              # 1000 recommended for a full run
    type = "case",             # case-dropping method
    statistics = c("bridgeExpectedInfluence"), # test Bridge EI only
    communities = communities, # pass the dynamic communities
    nCores = 8,                # multi-core speedup (adjust to your machine)
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  # 5. Compute the CS-coefficient
  # cor = 0.7 is the standard threshold (CS > 0.25 acceptable, > 0.5 excellent)
  cor_stab <- corStability(boot_res, cor = 0.7)
  cs_value <- cor_stab[1] # extract the CS value for Bridge EI
  
  message(paste("   📊 CS-coefficient (Bridge EI):", round(cs_value, 3)))
  
  # 5. Plot and save
  pdf_filename <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Stability_CS_", model_label, ".pdf"))
  pdf(pdf_filename, width = 10, height = 6)
  
  p <- plot(boot_res, statistics = "bridgeExpectedInfluence") + 
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste("Stability of Bridge EI -", model_label),
         subtitle = paste("CS-coefficient (cor=0.7) =", round(cs_value, 3)),
         caption = "Criteria: CS > 0.25 is acceptable; CS > 0.5 is stable.") + 
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face="bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  message(paste("   ✅ Saved plot to:", basename(pdf_filename)))
}

message("\n🎉 PHASE 3 ALL COMPLETED! Check your output folder.")
```




# Analysis 3: DAG three steps
```{r}

library(bnlearn)
library(bootnet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# IV. PHASE 2: DAG ANALYSIS (Based on SES-Adjusted Residuals)
# ==============================================================================
message("\n🚀 STARTING PHASE 2: DAG ANALYSIS")

# Ensure output directories exist
if(!exists("out_dir_dag")) out_dir_dag <- file.path(out_dir, "DAG_Analysis")
if(!dir.exists(out_dir_dag)) dir.create(out_dir_dag, recursive = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Core computation and raw-object save (computation & save raw RDS)
# ==============================================================================

message("\n🚀 [Step 1] STARTING HEAVY COMPUTATION (Bootstrap on Residuals)")
message(paste("📂 Output Directory:", out_dir_dag))

# Check that df_resid exists
if(!exists("df_resid")) stop("Error: df_resid does not exist. Run Step 4 first.")

target_models <- names(multi_models) 

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  message(paste(">>> [Computing] Running Bootstrap for:", model_label))
  
  # --- A. Data preparation (using the deconfounded residuals) ---
  nodes_extra <- multi_models[[model_label]]
  node_names_model <- c(e_names, l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  dat_resid_sub <- df_resid %>% 
    dplyr::select(all_of(node_names_model))
  
  # --- B. Blacklist setup (tiered blacklist) ---
  # Forbid: Lifestyle -> Environment
  # Forbid: Health    -> Environment
  
  non_env_nodes <- c(l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  black_list <- expand.grid(from = non_env_nodes, to = e_names, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  # --- C. Core computation (bootstrapping) ---
  tryCatch({
  # Fix the DAG bootstrap seed
    set.seed(999)
    
    start_time <- Sys.time()
    
    # Core computation: R=500 (raise to 500 or 1000 for stable results), alpha=0.01
    # Use the PC-stable algorithm
    str_fit <- boot.strength(
      data = dat_resid_sub, 
      R = 500,    # <--- recommendation: use 500 or 1000 for publication
      algorithm = "pc.stable",
      algorithm.args = list(
        blacklist = black_list, 
        alpha = 0.01  # significance level
      )
    ) 
    
    end_time <- Sys.time()
    duration <- round(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs"), 1)
    message(paste("   ⏱️ Computation finished in", duration, "seconds."))
    
    # --- D. Save the raw object (.rds) ---
    rds_filename <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
    saveRDS(str_fit, file = rds_filename)
    
    message(paste("   💾 Saved Raw RDS:", rds_filename))
    
  }, error = function(e){
    message(paste("   ❌ Error in calculation for", model_label, ":", e$message))
  })
}

message("\n✅ [Step 1] ALL COMPUTATIONS DONE. Raw data saved to .rds files.")
message("👉 Next: Run 'Step 2' (Sensitivity) and 'Step 3' (Plotting).")

```



```{r}
library(bnlearn)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) # ggplot2 is used for the line plot

library(bnlearn)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) 

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Sensitivity analysis (with CSV export and elbow plot) - extended
# ==============================================================================

message("\n📊 [Step 2] STARTING SENSITIVITY CHECK & PLOTTING")

# Define the test range
test_thresholds <- sort(unique(c(seq(0.70, 0.95, by = 0.05), 0.98)))

# Define the thresholds for which a CSV should be exported
export_targets <- c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95)

target_models <- names(multi_models)

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  # --- 1. Read the RDS file saved in Step 1 ---
  rds_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
  
  if(!file.exists(rds_file)){
    message(paste("⚠️ Skipped:", model_label, "(RDS file not found)"))
    next
  }
  
  message(paste("\n>>> Analyzing Model:", model_label))
  str_fit <- readRDS(rds_file)
  
  # --- 2. Loop over thresholds and count edges ---
  results_list <- list()
  
  for(th in test_thresholds){
    # Compute the averaged network
    avg <- averaged.network(str_fit, threshold = th)
    # Count the edges
    final_arcs <- as.data.frame(avg$arcs)
    num_edges <- nrow(final_arcs)
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # If this is a target threshold (85, 90, 95), save a CSV immediately
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    if(th %in% export_targets){
      # example filename: DAG_Arrows_0.9_Mental_Health.csv
      arrow_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("DAG_Arrows_", th, "_", model_label, ".csv"))
      
      if(num_edges > 0){
        write.csv(final_arcs, arrow_file, row.names = FALSE)
        message(paste0("      💾 [Export] Saved arrows for threshold ", th, " (Edges: ", num_edges, ")"))
      } else {
        message(paste0("      ⚠️ [Export] Threshold ", th, " has 0 edges, skip saving."))
      }
    }
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Auto-generate a description (for reference only)
    desc <- ""
    if(num_edges > 100) desc <- "Very Dense"
    else if(num_edges > 50) desc <- "Dense"
    else if(num_edges >= 20) desc <- "Moderate (Interpretable)"
    else if(num_edges > 5) desc <- "Sparse (Skeleton)"
    else desc <- "Very Sparse"
    
    # Store in the list
    results_list[[as.character(th)]] <- data.frame(
      Threshold = th,
      Edge_Count = num_edges,
      Description = desc,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # Combine into a data frame
  df_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  
  # --- 3. Export the summary CSV (for the supplement) ---
  csv_name <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Sensitivity_Table_", model_label, ".csv"))
  write.csv(df_results, csv_name, row.names = FALSE)
  message(paste("   💾 Summary Table Saved:", csv_name))
  
  # --- 4. Draw the line plot (scree plot) ---
  p <- ggplot(df_results, aes(x = Threshold, y = Edge_Count)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.2) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Edge_Count), vjust = -0.8, size = 3.5) +
    # Mark the 0.85 and 0.90 positions
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.85, 0.90, 0.95), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = test_thresholds) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Sensitivity Analysis:", model_label),
      subtitle = "Number of Edges vs. Inclusion Threshold",
      x = "Threshold (Bootstrap Confidence)",
      y = "Number of Edges (Complexity)"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
    )
  
  plot_name <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Sensitivity_Plot_", model_label, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(plot_name, plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
  message(paste("   📈 Plot Saved:", plot_name))
}

message("\n✅ [Step 2] Analysis Done.")
message("👉 Checked Output folder for new 'DAG_Arrows_0.XX_....csv' files.")
```

# DAG_Layered plot
library(qgraph)
library(dplyr)
library(bnlearn)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: Final plotting (debug-fixed - resolves node-name mismatch)
# ==============================================================================

FINAL_THRESHOLD <- 0.70

message(paste("\n🎨 [Step 3 Debug] STARTING PLOTTING | Threshold:", FINAL_THRESHOLD))

target_models <- names(multi_models) 

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  # --- 1. Read the raw data ---
  rds_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
  
  if(!file.exists(rds_file)){
    message(paste("⚠️ Skipped:", model_label, "(RDS not found)"))
    next
  }
  
  str_fit <- readRDS(rds_file)
  
  # --- 2. Filter edges ---
  avg_dag <- averaged.network(str_fit, threshold = FINAL_THRESHOLD)
  final_arcs <- as.data.frame(avg_dag$arcs)
  
  all_nodes <- nodes(avg_dag) 
  n_total <- length(all_nodes)
  
  # --- Diagnostic report ---
  message(paste0("\n>>> [Diagnostic] Model: ", model_label))
  message(paste0("    1. Theoretical Edges (from Table): ", nrow(final_arcs)))
  message(paste0("    2. Total Nodes found: ", n_total))
  if(nrow(final_arcs) > 0){
    message(paste0("    3. First edge sample: ", final_arcs[1,1], " -> ", final_arcs[1,2]))
    message(paste0("    4. First node name:   ", all_nodes[1]))
  }
  
  # --- 3. Prepare the plotting matrices ---
  # A. Adjacency matrix
  dag_adj <- matrix(0, nrow = n_total, ncol = n_total)
  rownames(dag_adj) <- colnames(dag_adj) <- all_nodes
  
  # B. Edge-colour matrix
  edge_col_mat <- matrix("black", nrow = n_total, ncol = n_total)
  rownames(edge_col_mat) <- colnames(edge_col_mat) <- all_nodes 
  
  get_group_id_safe <- function(node_name_clean){
    
    
    
    e_names_safe <- make.names(e_names)
    l_names_safe <- make.names(l_names)
    
    if(node_name_clean %in% e_names || node_name_clean %in% e_names_safe) return(1)
    if(node_name_clean %in% l_names || node_name_clean %in% l_names_safe) return(2)
    return(3) # everything else is Health
  }
  
  # --- 4. Fill the matrices ---
  matches_count <- 0
  if(nrow(final_arcs) > 0){
    for(i in 1:nrow(final_arcs)){
      f <- final_arcs[i, "from"]
      t <- final_arcs[i, "to"]
      
      if(f %in% all_nodes && t %in% all_nodes){
        dag_adj[f, t] <- 1
        matches_count <- matches_count + 1
        
        g_src <- get_group_id_safe(f)
        g_dst <- get_group_id_safe(t)
        
        if(g_src == g_dst) edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "gray80"      
        else if(g_src < g_dst) edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "forestgreen" 
        else edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "firebrick2"  
      }
    }
  }
  message(paste0("    5. Edges successfully plotted: ", matches_count, " / ", nrow(final_arcs)))

  # --- 5. Build the layered layout (adapted to the new names) ---
  Layout_Matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_total, ncol = 2)
  
  group_ids <- sapply(all_nodes, get_group_id_safe)
  
  idx_e <- which(group_ids == 1)
  idx_l <- which(group_ids == 2)
  idx_h <- which(group_ids == 3)
  
  # E (Top)
  if(length(idx_e) > 0){
    Layout_Matrix[idx_e, 1] <- seq(-2.4, 2.4, length.out = length(idx_e))
    Layout_Matrix[idx_e, 2] <- 1.0
  }
  # L (Mid)
  if(length(idx_l) > 0){
    Layout_Matrix[idx_l, 1] <- seq(-1.6, 1.6, length.out = length(idx_l))
    Layout_Matrix[idx_l, 2] <- 0.0
  }
  # H (Bot)
  if(length(idx_h) > 0){
    Layout_Matrix[idx_h, 1] <- seq(-0.8, 0.8, length.out = length(idx_h))
    Layout_Matrix[idx_h, 2] <- -1.0
  }

  # --- 5. Plot ---
  # Community list
  groups_model <- list("Environment" = 1:n_e, "Lifestyle" = (n_e + 1):(n_e + n_l))
  groups_model[[model_label]] <- (n_e + n_l + 1):(n_e + n_l + n_h)
  current_colors <- custom_node_colors[names(groups_model)]

  tryCatch({
    pdf(file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("DAG_Layered_", model_label, ".pdf")), width = 32, height = 16)
    
    qgraph(dag_adj, 
           layout = Layout_Matrix, # not "spring"; pass the coordinate matrix directly
           
           rescale = TRUE,         # auto-rescale to fit the canvas
           
           # === Style ===
           edge.color = edge_col_mat, 
           groups = groups_model,           
           color = current_colors, 
           labels = colnames(dag_adj), 
           vsize = 2.5,
           label.cex = 0.8,
           border.color = "gray30",
           
           nodeNames = NULL,
           legend = TRUE, 
           legend.cex = 0.5,
           
           directed = TRUE,
           mode = "direct",
           esize = 1.2,
           asize = 2.0,
           
           curve = 0.3,     # 0 = straight; larger = more curved
           curveAll = TRUE, # curve all edges to avoid passing through middle nodes
           
           title = paste("DAG Structure (Layered):", model_label),
           title.cex = 1.6,
           mar = c(9, 5, 5, 3)
    )
    
    mtext(param_label_1, side = 1, line = 3, adj = 0, cex = 0.85, col = "gray40", font = 3)
    mtext(param_label_2, side = 1, line = 4.5, adj = 0, cex = 0.85, col = "gray40", font = 3)
    
    dev.off()
    message(paste("   ✅ Layered Plot Saved:", model_label))
    
  }, error = function(e){
    message(paste("   ❌ Error:", e$message))
    if(dev.cur() > 1) dev.off()
  })

}
